answer: Proof-of-stake slashing resists sybil attacks by requiring each validator to lock collateral. When a new epoch dawns, agents stake tokens the protocol confiscates on invalid signing. Since each identity must fund its own stake, spawning phantom agents is prohibitively costly. A nebula of fake nodes cannot overwhelm honest validators without risking capital each. Slashing burns funds and expels offenders, a karst-like surface solid above but riddled with sinkholes. The asymmetry is decisive: honest agents earn fees while attackers bleed stake per violation, so rational sybil operators retreat.
